title: BELA Act 3: Admission and language policy
description: What the BELA Act changed about admission and language policies in public schools: the SGB's role, the HOD's new powers, the factors, appeals and what is still in draft.

lessons.title: Admission policy: who decides what
lessons.summary: The SGB still writes the admission policy, but the HOD now has the final say on admitting a learner.
lessons.body:
## 🎯 Why this lesson matters

Admissions cause more parent complaints than almost anything else an SGB deals with. The BELA Act (Basic Education Laws Amendment Act 32 of 2024) rewrote the admission rules in section 5 of the South African Schools Act 84 of 1996 (SASA). These rules apply to **public schools only**. Independent schools follow their own admission rules and their board of governors' policies.

BELA 1 covers when the Act started. In short: the whole Act, including the admission and language sections, has been in force since 24 December 2024.

## 🏫 The starting point: a public school must admit

SASA s5(1), as substituted by BELA s4(a), now says a public school must admit learners, provide education to them and serve their educational requirements for the whole time they attend, without unfairly discriminating in any way.

BELA s4(b) added two practical rules:

- **s5(1A):** a learner whose parent or guardian has not provided the required documents during the application must still be allowed to attend school.
- **s5(1B):** the principal must advise the parent or guardian to get the required documents.

> 💡 Tip: Missing a birth certificate or proof of address is no longer a reason to keep a child out of class. Let the learner attend, and put the principal's advice to the parent in writing.

## 📝 The SGB still determines the admission policy

Despite talk that "the department takes over admissions", SASA s5(5), as substituted by BELA s4(d), says that, subject to SASA and any applicable provincial law, the admission policy of a public school **is determined by the governing body**, in line with the Constitution and relevant legislation.

The final Act does not say the policy must be sent to the Head of Department (HOD) for approval before it is valid. What it adds are three provisos.

### 1️⃣ Factors the SGB must weigh (s5(5)(a))

When it considers the policy or an amendment for approval, the SGB must be satisfied that the policy takes into account the needs, in general, of the broader community in the education district where the school is situated. It must take into account factors including, but not limited to:

1. the best interests of the child, with emphasis on equality (section 9 of the Constitution) and equity;
2. whether there are other schools in the community that are accessible to learners;
3. the available resources of the school and the efficient and effective use of state resources; and
4. the space available at the school for learners.

The list is a minimum: "including, but not limited to".

### 2️⃣ The HOD has the final authority to admit (s5(5)(b))

The HOD, after consultation with the SGB, has the final authority to admit a learner to a public school, subject to the appeal right in s5(9). So the SGB writes the rules, but the decision on an individual learner rests with the HOD.

### 3️⃣ Regular review (s5(5)(c))

The SGB must review the admission policy:

- every three years;
- whenever the factors in s5(5)(a) have changed, when circumstances so require; or
- at the request of the HOD.

> ⚠️ Watch out: "After consultation with the SGB" means the HOD must genuinely consult, but the HOD does not need the SGB's agreement. If the SGB disagrees, its remedy is an appeal to the MEC (covered in the next lesson).

## 🗂️ What this looks like at an SGB meeting

Imagine your SGB is updating its feeder-zone rules. A good minute records that the SGB looked at each of the four factors: the child's best interests, the other accessible schools nearby, the school's resources, and the classroom space. Attach the enrolment figures you relied on. If the policy is ever challenged, that minute is your proof that the SGB did what s5(5)(a) requires.

## ✅ Key points

- SASA s5(5) (as substituted by BELA s4(d)) keeps the admission policy with the SGB of a public school.
- The SGB must weigh the broader community's needs and at least the four listed factors.
- The HOD, after consulting the SGB, has the final authority to admit a learner.
- The policy must be reviewed every three years, when the factors change, or when the HOD asks.
- A learner without documents must still be allowed to attend (s5(1A)).

lessons.title: Admission refusals and appeals
lessons.summary: Fixed 14-day appeal windows for parents and for the SGB, and what happens to the policy while an appeal runs.
lessons.body:
## ⏱️ The new 14-day clock

BELA s4(e) and s4(f) rewrote the appeal rules in SASA s5 for public schools. Appeals now run on 14-day clocks, and the SGB itself has a right to appeal.

## 👪 When a parent's application is refused

### The parent's appeal (s5(9))

Any learner, or parent of a learner, who has been refused admission to a public school may appeal against the decision to the Member of the Executive Council (MEC) for education **within 14 days of receiving the notification of the refusal**.

### The MEC's deadline (s5(10))

Once the appeal is received, the MEC must, **within 14 days**, consider and decide the matter and inform the learner or the parent of the outcome.

> 💡 Tip: A parent can only count 14 days if they know when they were told. Make sure every refusal letter is dated, clearly explains that the parent may appeal to the MEC, and is delivered in a way you can prove (email, SMS record, or a signed receipt).

## 🏛️ When the SGB disagrees with the HOD

Remember from Lesson 1 that the HOD, after consulting the SGB, has the final authority to admit a learner (s5(5)(b)). What if the HOD places a learner in a way the SGB believes breaks the school's policy?

- **s5(11):** if the SGB is not satisfied with the HOD's decision under s5(5)(b), the SGB may appeal to the MEC within **14 days after receiving** the HOD's decision.
- **s5(12):** the MEC must, within **14 days** of receiving that appeal, consider and decide it and inform the SGB of the outcome.

### The policy stays alive during the appeal (s5(13))

While the MEC considers the appeal, the admission policy remains valid and applicable. Only the provisions that are the subject of the appeal are suspended until the appeal is finalised. So an appeal about one clause does not freeze the whole policy.

> ⚠️ Watch out: An SGB appeal is a formal decision of the governing body. Take a proper resolution at a quorate meeting, record the reasons, and send the appeal in writing well inside the 14 days. A letter from one member acting alone may be challenged.

## 🤝 Appeals versus the new dispute process

BELA s37 inserted a general dispute resolution procedure in SASA s59A for disputes between the HOD and an SGB (informal talks, then written notice, then nominated representatives, then an appeal to the MEC). However, s59A(3) says that procedure **does not apply** where the Act already provides an appeal process. Admission refusals and HOD admission decisions have their own appeal in s5(9) and s5(11), so use those, not s59A. BELA 4 covers s59A in more detail.

## 🚫 False information is now an offence

BELA s36 added s59(3) to SASA. If a parent or any other person, when applying for admission to a public school:

- submits information they know is false or misleading;
- submits a document they know is forged; or
- claims a document is a true copy of the original when it is not,

that person commits an offence and on conviction may be fined or imprisoned for up to 12 months, or both. The same applies to applications for exemption from school fees.

## 🧭 A worked example

A parent refused a Grade 8 place has 14 days from receiving the letter to appeal, and the MEC has 14 days to decide. Separately, the HOD places another learner after consulting the SGB, and the SGB believes this ignores the space limit. It resolves to appeal within 14 days of receiving the HOD's decision, and the rest of its policy keeps working meanwhile.

## ✅ Key points

- A refused learner or parent may appeal to the MEC within 14 days of receiving the refusal (s5(9)).
- The MEC must decide a parent's appeal within 14 days of receiving it (s5(10)).
- The SGB may appeal an HOD admission decision to the MEC within 14 days, and the MEC has 14 days to decide (s5(11) and (12)).
- During an appeal only the challenged parts of the policy are suspended (s5(13)).
- Giving false information or forged documents in an admission application is an offence (s59(3)).

lessons.title: Language policy and the HOD's directive
lessons.summary: The SGB still sets the language policy, but the HOD may direct a school to add a language of instruction after a full public process.
lessons.body:
## 🌍 What changed in section 6

BELA s5 amended SASA s6 (language policy in **public schools**). The SGB still determines the policy, but there are new factors, a review cycle, and a new HOD power to direct a school to adopt more than one language of instruction.

## 📝 The SGB still determines the policy (s6(2))

The governing body of a public school may, subject to s6(7), determine the school's language policy, subject to the Constitution, SASA and any applicable provincial law. The language policy must be limited to one or more of the official languages of the Republic listed in section 6(1) of the Constitution.

### South African Sign Language (s6(4))

BELA s5(b) changed s6(4): South African Sign Language now has the status of an official language for purposes of learning at a public school.

## 🧮 Factors the SGB must weigh (s6(5))

When determining the language policy or an amendment, the SGB must be satisfied that it takes into account the language needs, in general, of the broader community in the education district. It must take into account factors including, but not limited to:

1. the best interests of the child, with emphasis on equality (section 9 of the Constitution) and equity;
2. section 6(2) of the Constitution (the state's duty to elevate the status and advance the use of indigenous languages);
3. section 29(2) of the Constitution (the right to be taught in the official language of choice where reasonably practicable);
4. the changing number of learners who speak the language of learning and teaching at the school;
5. the need for effective use of classroom space and resources of the school; and
6. the enrolment trends of the school.

### Review (s6(6))

The SGB must review the language policy every three years, or whenever the factors in s6(5) have changed, when circumstances so require, or at the request of the HOD.

## 🧭 The HOD's power to direct more than one language (s6(7) and (8))

Despite the SGB's power in s6(2), the HOD may, where it is practicable and subject to s6(5), direct a public school to adopt more than one language of instruction. In deciding practicability the HOD must consider factors including the child's best interests, the changing number of learners speaking the language of learning and teaching, effective use of space and resources, and the community's language needs (s6(8)).

## 📣 The process the HOD must follow (s6(9) to (11))

The HOD may not issue a directive unless he or she has:

1. informed the school and the SGB in writing of the intention and the reasons;
2. notified parents and the community (a local newspaper notice if any circulate, a notice sent home with every learner, and other acceptable means);
3. given the school, SGB, parents and community a reasonable opportunity to make representations;
4. held a public hearing on reasonable notice; and
5. given due consideration to the representations received.

The HOD must then inform the school and SGB of the decision and reasons, and notify parents and the community (s6(10)). Before the directive is implemented, the HOD must take all necessary steps to make sure the school receives the necessary resources, including educators and learning and teaching support material, to provide adequate tuition in the additional language (s6(11)).

> ⚠️ Watch out: If the department signals an intention under s6(7), the SGB's best moment to influence the outcome is during the representations and public hearing. Prepare evidence: enrolment trends, classroom space and staffing.

## 🏛️ The SGB's appeal (s6(12) to (14))

If the SGB is not satisfied with the directive, it may appeal to the MEC within 14 days after receiving it. The MEC must decide within 14 days of receiving the appeal and inform the SGB. While the appeal is considered, the language policy remains valid and only the provisions under appeal are suspended.

## ✅ Key points

- The SGB of a public school still determines the language policy, limited to official languages (s6(2)).
- South African Sign Language has official-language status for learning at a public school (s6(4)).
- The SGB must weigh at least the six factors in s6(5) and review the policy every three years or when needed (s6(6)).
- The HOD may direct a school to add a language of instruction only after the full s6(9) process, and must supply resources first (s6(11)).
- The SGB may appeal a directive to the MEC within 14 days (s6(12)).

lessons.title: What is current: regulations, guidelines and your to-do list
lessons.summary: What has and has not been finalised for admissions and language, and the practical steps an SGB should take now.
lessons.body:
## 📌 The law is already in force

Sections 4 and 5 of the BELA Act, which amend SASA s5 (admission) and s6 (language), are in force. BELA 1 explains the commencement history. The Department of Basic Education (DBE) has repeatedly said that publishing regulations does not pause implementation: the amended sections apply now.

## 📜 Regulations: what BELA allows and where things stand

BELA s39 amended SASA s61 so the Minister may make regulations, among other things, on the admission of learners to public schools (s61(1)(aB)). Under the new s61(3), any regulation on admissions must be tabled in Parliament **before** it is published in the Gazette.

What we could verify as at October 2026:

- **6 August 2025:** the Minister published two sets of **draft** regulations for public comment, one on school admissions and one on minimum uniform norms and standards for the capacity of ordinary public schools. Reports say the comment period was later extended into January 2026.
- **7 August 2026:** the DBE published a further four draft instruments (SGB elections, additional remuneration of state employees under s38A, teacher development centres, and the national education information system). None of these is the admissions regulation.
- We found **no notice of final admission regulations** being published. There are also no national language-policy regulations; the language rules come straight from SASA s6.

> ⚠️ Watch out: This area is moving. Before your SGB relies on any "new admission regulations", ask your district office for the Government Gazette notice number and confirm it is the final version, not a draft.

## 📘 The Minister's implementation guidelines

In June 2025 the Minister released implementation guidelines on admission and language policy. News reports state that they were not gazetted as regulations, and teacher unions disputed their legal weight. Treat them as guidance on how the department intends to act, not as law. The Act itself (SASA s5 and s6) is what binds the SGB and the HOD.

## 🗺️ Provincial rules still apply

Both s5(5) and s6(2) say the SGB acts "subject to" SASA and any applicable provincial law. Provinces have their own admission regulations, application systems and annual admission circulars (Gauteng, for example, runs online applications). Those continue to apply alongside BELA. Your district office can tell you which provincial regulation and circular is current for this year.

> 💡 Tip: Keep a one-page "admissions source list": SASA s5, your provincial regulations, this year's circular, and your policy with its review date.

## ✅ The SGB's to-do list

1. **Check your review dates.** Admission and language policies must be reviewed at least every three years (s5(5)(c) and s6(6)). Diarise the next review.
2. **Review against the factors.** Walk through the four admission factors in s5(5)(a) and the six language factors in s6(5) item by item, and minute your reasoning.
3. **Use real data.** Enrolment trends, waiting lists, classroom space and the number of learners speaking each language are evidence the Act expects you to consider.
4. **Fix your refusal letters.** Every refusal should be dated and explain the 14-day appeal right to the MEC (s5(9)).
5. **Plan for appeals.** Agree in advance who drafts an SGB appeal and how a special meeting can be called quickly enough to meet a 14-day deadline (s5(11) and s6(12)).
6. **Respond to HOD requests.** If the HOD asks for a review, that triggers a review duty under s5(5)(c) or s6(6).
7. **Watch for final regulations.** When admissions regulations are finalised, your policy may need updating.

## 🧩 A quick example

The district writes asking your SGB to review its language policy because the number of isiZulu-speaking learners has grown. That request triggers the duty to review under s6(6). It is not yet a directive under s6(7). The SGB should hold the review, consider the s6(5) factors, and minute its decision. A directive could only follow after the full notice, representations and public hearing process in s6(9).

## ✅ Key points

- The admission and language amendments are in force now; regulations add detail but are not needed for the Act to apply.
- Admission regulations must be tabled in Parliament before publication (s61(3)).
- As at October 2026 the admissions and capacity regulations we found were still drafts; confirm the current status with your district office.
- The Minister's 2025 guidelines are guidance, not law.
- Diarise policy reviews, minute the factors, and prepare for 14-day appeal deadlines.

questions.text: Under SASA s5(5) as substituted by the BELA Act, who determines the admission policy of a public school?

options.text: The governing body of the school
The Head of Department
The MEC for education
The principal, after consulting the district office

questions.explanation: SASA s5(5), as substituted by BELA s4(d), says the admission policy of a public school is determined by its governing body, subject to SASA and any applicable provincial law.

questions.text: Who has the final authority to admit a learner to a public school?

options.text: The SGB, by majority vote
The Head of Department, after consultation with the SGB
The principal acting alone
The MEC, after consulting the parents

questions.explanation: SASA s5(5)(b), as substituted by BELA s4(d), gives the HOD, after consultation with the governing body, the final authority to admit a learner, subject to the appeal in s5(9).

questions.text: A parent applies for a place but has not yet provided the learner's birth certificate. What does the Act now require?

options.text: The application must be rejected until all documents are received
The learner may attend for 14 days only
The SGB must decide at its next meeting whether the learner may attend
The learner must be allowed to attend, and the principal must advise the parent to get the documents

questions.explanation: SASA s5(1A) and (1B), inserted by BELA s4(b), say a learner whose parent has not provided required documents must still be allowed to attend, and the principal must advise the parent to secure them.

questions.text: A parent receives a refusal letter. Within what period may they appeal to the MEC?

options.text: Within 14 days of receiving the notification of the refusal
Within 7 days of the refusal decision being taken
Within 30 days of receiving the notification
Within 21 days of the start of the school year

questions.explanation: SASA s5(9), as substituted by BELA s4(e), gives a refused learner or parent 14 days from receiving the notification of refusal to appeal to the MEC.

questions.text: While the MEC considers an SGB's appeal against an HOD admission decision, what happens to the school's admission policy?

options.text: The whole policy is suspended until the appeal is decided
The HOD's version of the policy replaces it
It stays valid, and only the provisions under appeal are suspended
It lapses and must be re-adopted after the appeal

questions.explanation: SASA s5(13), added by BELA s4(f), says the admission policy remains valid and applicable while the MEC considers the appeal; only the provisions that are the subject of the appeal are suspended.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT one of the factors listed in SASA s5(5)(a) that an SGB must take into account for its admission policy?

options.text: The best interests of the child, with emphasis on equality and equity
The school's results in the previous year's national examinations
Whether there are other accessible schools in the community
The space available at the school for learners

questions.explanation: SASA s5(5)(a) lists the best interests of the child, other accessible schools, available resources and efficient use of state resources, and available space. Examination results are not a listed factor.

questions.text: When may the HOD direct a public school to adopt more than one language of instruction?

options.text: Whenever 10 learners request a language
Only with the written agreement of the SGB
Only if the MEC first amends the school's language policy
Where it is practicable, after the notice, representations and public hearing process in s6(9)

questions.explanation: SASA s6(7) and (9), added by BELA s5(c), allow the HOD to direct more than one language of instruction where practicable, but only after written notice, community notice, representations, a public hearing and due consideration.

questions.text: Before an HOD's language directive is implemented, what must the HOD do under SASA s6(11)?

options.text: Obtain a court order
Take all necessary steps to make sure the school receives resources such as educators and learning materials
Dissolve and re-elect the SGB
Wait three years for the next policy review

questions.explanation: SASA s6(11), added by BELA s5(c), requires the HOD, before the directive is implemented, to ensure the school receives the necessary resources, including educators and learning and teaching support material.

questions.text: How often must an SGB review its language policy, as a minimum?

options.text: Every year before the budget meeting
Every five years
Every three years, and also when the factors change, when circumstances require, or at the HOD's request
Only when the HOD issues a directive

questions.explanation: SASA s6(6), added by BELA s5(c), requires review every three years or whenever the s6(5) factors have changed, when circumstances so require, or at the request of the HOD.

questions.text: Which statement about national admission regulations under SASA s61 is correct?

options.text: They must be tabled in Parliament before publication, and the 2025 versions published for comment were drafts
They were finalised together with the Act on 13 September 2024
They are optional and cannot override provincial law in any way
They can be made by each MEC without the Minister

questions.explanation: BELA s39 inserted s61(1)(aB) (regulations on admission) and s61(3), which requires admission regulations to be tabled in Parliament before publication. The admissions and capacity regulations published on 6 August 2025 were drafts for public comment.
